headline: Is he hiding something from me?
note: HIDING-SOMETHING. A real man exists here and may be referred to as she refers to him, but nothing in the read rules on him. Guard inherited verbatim from the live tarot hook of the same headline. (1) NEVER STATE THAT HE IS HIDING SOMETHING AND NEVER STATE THAT HE IS NOT. Both are verdicts on a real man drawn off a cup she tapped on an ad, and the second also tells her that what she noticed was never there — which is exactly what she has already been told, by him or by friends. Cut 2 carries the word 'hiding' because it is quoting HER question back; no other bubble asserts anything about him. (2) NEVER NAME OR GUESS THE CONTENTS: not another woman, not money, not a secret past, not a feeling he will not admit. Supplying any of it is invention, and inventing it manufactures a crisis inside a relationship that is still running. (3) NEVER HAND HER A TACTIC: no checking his phone, messages or whereabouts, no testing him, no trap, and equally no ultimatum and no stepping back to provoke a reaction. (4) NEVER PATHOLOGISE HER WATCHFULNESS — no paranoid, insecure, anxious, obsessive, overthinking — and never diagnose him as secretive or avoidant as a character. WHERE IT LANDS: meeting an edge is not the same as imagining one. The three fears answered at cut 3 are: I made it up (bird), I am being asked to trust what I cannot see (tree), I can never reach it (anchor). ARM B — SHE NAMES THE SYMBOL, SO CUT 1 CONFIRMS AND PLACES IT; IT DOES NOT REVEAL IT. On arm A the cup was unreadable and cut 1 was the payoff: Evelyn saw what she could not. Here she has already tapped 'A. Bird' on a lander showing one cup, so telling her there is a bird in it reveals nothing. Cut 1 agrees with her and adds the half she could not have: WHERE it sits. Every position word is measured off the actual photograph (improve-v1/fb-read/images/armb/SOURCE.md) — bird at 3.4 o'clock on the handle side, tree at 7.4 with its roots running inward, anchor at 10.4 opposite the handle. All three sit halfway up the wall, so on this cup the meaning is carried by WHICH SIDE and never by depth: nothing may be read as near the rim or down in the middle, because nothing is. DEVICE RULES: the handle side is hers, the far side is what comes from outside her, and the system is never explained to her — she should feel the position mean something, never be taught it. The bird is a picture and never gets intent or motion; the tree does not grow while she watches; the anchor does not drop. The moment any of them moves, the leaves have quietly become a man doing something. NOTHING INVENTED ABOUT HER WAKING LIFE: no gesture, habit, routine, count, age or event, and for this device nothing about how she drinks her tea, how often, with whom, or whether she has had a reading before. The leaves are in the picture; what she brought is what she typed; nothing else is ours to assert. CUT 3 ANSWERS FLAT, and the three cut-3 lines answer three different fears so the panels do not collapse into one sentence said three ways. CUT 6 RECOGNISES AND NEVER RE-ASKS — cut 2 already echoes the ad question, so cut 6 hands back something she has lived, drawn only from her question and from what cuts 1-5 established in the cup.

voc.why: inherits the shipped tarot cards-hiding-something finding and its guard

a: A bird, yes. Wings out, halfway up your cup, and over on the handle side.
You asked whether he's hiding something from you. A bird is word, and yours stopped on your side of the cup.
You met an edge. Meeting one is not the same as imagining one, whatever you've been told.
The bird doesn't say what's past it. Nothing in the leaves names what sits on the other side.
So the word came as far as your side and no further, and you've been filling in the rest yourself.
You noticed something and then had to argue yourself out of it, dear. That's the tiring part.
Let me look closer at what's been stopping the word halfway…
b: A tree, yes. Halfway up the cup, with its roots running toward the middle.
You asked whether he's hiding something from you. A tree shows you its top, and the roots run where you can't see.
There's a part of this you can't see from where you stand. That's the shape of it, and you didn't put it there.
What's under the ground stays under it. The leaves don't tell me one thing about what's down there.
So you can see the whole tree and still not know the half of it.
You've been asked to take the top of it on trust, dear, and something in you won't.
Let me look closer at what's keeping so much of this underground…
c: An anchor, yes. Halfway up the cup, on the far side from the handle.
You asked whether he's hiding something from you. An anchor holds, and yours sits over on the far side, out of reach.
There's a place where what you're told stops. You keep arriving at it, and it's real.
The anchor sits on the far side. Nothing in the leaves tells me what it's holding down.
So something's fixed over there, and you've never once been able to get to it.
You've had to keep steady on your own side of this, dear, without a thing to stand on.
Let me look closer at what's kept that anchor out of your reach…
